subject: [RFC PATCH 0/4] mm/zswap: make shrinker writeback work with iocost

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a kworker is already running on the same lruvec, and requested a check to prevent concurrent writeback operations.

The reviewer noted that the current implementation may not scale due to the lack of worker accumulation, and requested further testing and discussion.

Reviewer noted that the throttled writeback bio will incur debt in the cgroup and suggested deferring it until the cgroup has sufficient budget, as direct reclaimers would stall on application latency and kswapd reclaim would stall on a single cgroup's IO budget.

Reviewer noted that enabling the zswap shrinker results in a significant decrease (~97%) in the zswap pool size, which they believe acts as an additional throttling mechanism and may prevent 'hot' pages from being drained.

Reviewer noted that the work piled up in the shrinker control loop when writeback couldn't catch up, but considered this to be a desired behavior.

Reviewer noted that the current implementation could lead to starvation of other memory cgroups when one worker exhausts its memory budget, and suggested this as a reason for the performance issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Nhat,

On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 3:43 PM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:

---

It would not scale indeed, the worker does not accumulate in this
version of the patch. That needs to be tested and discussed.

---

Today the writeback bio is issued as root, which incurs debt to the
cgroup. The submitting task repays it on return to user or on any
other IO of the cgroup until the debt is paid off.

With this series the bio is throttled at submission instead, so
whoever submits it sleeps until the cgroup has budget:
- for direct reclaimers, that's the application latency we observed
- for kswapd reclaim, it would stall on a single cgroup's IO budget

So we need to defer for everyone.

---

In the large production workload I have worked on, when the shrinker
is enabled, the zswap pool size decreases by ~97%. So I did not want
to accumulate "too much" work to prevent zswap from draining "hot"
pages, it acts like an additional throttling mechanism. But that needs
discussion, hence the RFC.

And you're right, In the next version, I'll clearly point out all the
behavioral changes I made with their justifications.

---

Yes, this is another behavioural change that I will explain in the next version.

Indeed the work piles up in the shrinker control loop if writeback
cannot catch up but note that it is bounded, which is what we want
right?

---

You're right, and the explanation is "we cannot starve other memcgs if
one worker stalls because it exhausted its memcg budget".

Thanks Nhat!

Alex

2026-09-30.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the performance of zswap shrinker on systems running iocost by addressing two issues: (1) zswap writeback is issued as root and charged to the cgroup afterwards, causing stalls in application allocations; and (2) throttled writes sleep in their submitter, often an application thread. The patches modify zswap to mark writebacks as REQ_BACKGROUND instead of REQ_SWAP, allowing them to be throttled by iocost controllers. Additionally, patch 4 moves reclaim-driven writeback to a per-lruvec kworker, reducing the impact on application threads. The series includes benchmarks showing significant performance improvements for various workloads.

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: The reviewer questioned the necessity of REQ_SWAP and expressed concerns about the concept of REQ_SWAP, suggesting that non-swap paging can be just as important for forward progress.
reviews.raw_body:
The issue is that by definition it doesn't need REQ_SWAP then.

Then again the whole concept of REQ_SWAP looks sketchy to me, non-swap
paging can be just as important for forward progress, so if a driver
needs it, it has other issues anyway.
